findings.text: Rule 4 treats `._@.` in a printed name as proof of macro scopes, but the written declaration `def «x._@.y» := 0` contains that text and Lean returns `false` for `Name.hasMacroScopes`. Fix: Require `Name.hasMacroScopes` on the kernel name for both the helper and its candidate parent.

Rule 4 counts `arms_proc` as a second written declaration, although Lean generates `Parser.Attr.arms_proc` from the single written `register_simp_attr arms` command, so one source command can count as two users. Fix: Fold the generated parser into the declaration representing the written registration, or report it if its parent cannot be identified.

The rule accepts a successful reparse even when it changes the command boundary: a later postfix notation can make the parser consume the next command as part of the final `for` term and store both commands as the instance text. Fix: Require the boundary from the syntax active at the original command, or report the instance when that boundary cannot be established.

The missing-keyword rule discards a written `def` registered later by `attribute [instance]`, because its declaration range contains no `instance` keyword and belongs to no `deriving instance` command. Fix: Keep the full range of a written definition registered as an instance and apply the unresolved-command rule only when the defining command cannot be identified.

A generated constant whose parent was reported has no declaration to fold into, yet the next paragraph requires folding at both ends of every relationship and the prototype keeps such a target under its original name. Fix: Specify that the prototype omits the entity row and outgoing type and body relationships but retains incoming references under the unresolved target’s kernel name.
